```{r}
#| message: false
library(tidyverse)
```

Engine size and fuel economy often move in opposite directions. This graphic
shows highway mileage across vehicle classes, with a separate trend for each
drive type.

```{r}
ggplot(mpg, aes(x = displ, y = hwy, color = class)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.8, size = 2.5) +
  geom_smooth(aes(group = 1), color = "#263238", method = "loess",
              se = FALSE, linewidth = 1) +
  facet_wrap(vars(drv), labeller = as_labeller(c(
    f = "Front-wheel drive",
    r = "Rear-wheel drive",
    `4` = "4-wheel drive"
  ))) +
  scale_color_brewer(palette = "Set2", name = "Vehicle class") +
  labs(
    title = "Bigger engines, fewer highway miles",
    subtitle = "Highway fuel economy by engine size and drive type",
    x = "Engine size (liters)",
    y = "Highway fuel economy (miles per gallon)",
    caption = "Source: ggplot2::mpg"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(
    plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank()
  )
```
